claim: Germane load as a separate, independently measurable load type is not supported: no germane-specific instructional effect was generated in 25 years, and the 2019 and 2022 models fold it into redistribution of resources or the benefit side of total load.
agent_test: Do not build a germane budget knob; test only effects of reducing extraneous load or raising integration at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: '25 years' is the researcher's inference (Sweller 2023 says 'over the years'; 1998-2023); Sweller 2019/2023 and Skulmowski and Xu 2022 text all match.

claim: Questionnaire germane-load scales are reliable (pooled alpha .860, k=42) but weakly valid: GCL correlates only r=.17-.22 with retention/transfer (Leppink 2013 and Klepsch 2017 scales) and .40-.53 with intrinsic load; single-study evidence (Debue 2014) suggests GCL ratings may partly reflect immersion and enjoyment rather than schema building.
agent_test: Do not use self-rated or model-rated germane scores as a quality signal; use outcome accuracy.
audit_note: Alpha .860 (k=42), GCL-retention/transfer r=.173-.219 and ICL-GCL .403/.533 all match Krieglstein 2022, but 'largely tracks perceived effort or engagement' is not stated by the meta-analysis (engagement link comes from one separate study, Debue 2014).
claim_before_audit: Questionnaire germane-load scales are reliable (pooled alpha .860, k=42) but weakly valid: GCL correlates only r=.17-.22 with retention/transfer and .40-.53 with intrinsic load, so it largely tracks perceived effort or engagement.

claim: Germane ratings may reflect motivation and engagement, not schema building: GL-performance r=.045 (ns) but GL-immersion .36 and GL-enjoyment .40 (Debue N=128); naive raters did not separate low and high GCL tasks (Klepsch F(1,88)=0.04).
agent_test: Check whether an LLM's self-reported understanding predicts correctness beyond effort tokens.
audit_note: Debue numbers (r=.045, .362, .401, N=128) and Klepsch naive-rating null F(1,88)=0.04 p=.84 confirmed; claim is hedged with 'may'.

claim: The three-factor load structure fits ratings better than one factor in two studies (Klepsch CFI .970 vs .612; Jiang and Kalyuga CFI .994, N=60), but one germane item loaded only .28 and factors correlate; fit does not prove separate constructs. Re-read 2026-11: Klepsch Study 2 GCL alpha is only .67 with three items (.85 with two).
agent_test: Not directly testable on an agent.

claim: Support that explicitly helps integration works; support that merely 'increases germane load' or 'reduces extraneous load' does not: drawing-support meta-analysis g=0.35 with integration vs -0.15 without; GCL and ECL moderators ns (N=1213, 16 comparisons).
schema_part: O-operators on integration (states that force linking steps)
agent_test: Compare a scaffold that forces an explicit integrate step against one that only adds prompts of equal length.

claim: Variability and self-explanation help transfer only when total load is below capacity; for high-load learners the same activity hurts (expertise reversal; Cooper 2001 imagination).
agent_test: Run variable worked examples vs fixed examples on easy versus hard items at equal tokens.
audit_note: Sweller 2019 supports variability and self-explanation only within capacity and imagination only after expertise (Cooper 2001); 'hurts' is explicit only for variability with conventional problems; de Jong 2010 supports expertise-dependence.

claim: Counter-evidence: variability raised transfer without raising rated load (de Croock 1998), and learner-built organisers underperformed author-made ones (Stull and Mayer 2007), so germane-style effort is not reliably beneficial.
agent_test: Test self-generated vs supplied intermediate structure for an LLM at equal tokens.

claim: Extra supportive material can hurt when the target is already solved: skill-based in-context examples cost small models about 4% on easy MATH questions (cells down to -10.3 points); adaptive use gains up to 3.6% (AdaptMI) and 6% (AdaptMI+). Gating also works for DiffAdapt (1.5B-8B reasoning models, up to 22.4% fewer tokens, 9.7-10.1% for the 7B models, at comparable or improved accuracy) and cascades (up to +12% accuracy, up to 20% lower cost); frontier-model evidence for an adaptive gate is still missing, so the status holds for small and mid models only.
schema_part: O (example retrieval) with a difficulty gate
agent_test: Gate examples on a cheap difficulty estimate; compare with always-on at equal tokens.
audit_note: AdaptMI numbers confirmed (4% avg drop on easy MATH, -10.3 Precalculus Qwen2.5-1.5B, up to 3.6% and 6%) and cascade confirmed, but DiffAdapt tested 1.5B-8B models (not 4-8B) and 22.4% is the best-case saving (Qwen3-4B; 9.7-10.1% for 7B models) with 'comparable or improved' accuracy; DiffAdapt authors are Liu et al., not Chen et al.
claim_before_audit: Extra supportive material can hurt when the target is already solved: skill-based in-context examples cost small models about 4% on easy MATH questions (cells down to -10.3 points); adaptive use gains up to 3.6% (AdaptMI) and 6% (AdaptMI+). Gap search: gating also works for DiffAdapt (4-8B models, 22.4% fewer tokens at equal or better accuracy) and cascades (up to +12% accuracy, 20% lower cost); frontier-model evidence for an adaptive gate is still missing, so the status holds for small and mid models only.

claim: LLM accuracy falls as load rises: CogniLoad (22 models) 12 of 22 below 50% by d=5; steepest drop N=20 to 50 (DS-Llama-70B .89 to .66; Qwen3-8B .71 to .40); only gpt-5 .76 and o3 .68 above 50% at N=250; distractor ratio gives a U-shape.
agent_test: Vary step count and distractor ratio on our agent; test whether chunking holds accuracy at N=50 to 250.

claim: Multi-hop retrieval degrades with context-saturation load for one model only: Gemini-2.0-Flash EM .85 to .72 at 80% load (slope -0.003 per %), GPT-4o slope ns (p=.07), three open models at 0.00. Germane load was not measured.
agent_test: Replicate on our agent with padded context at equal tokens.

claim: Tool-use accuracy decays exponentially with a composite load score, with model-specific slopes (k 0.034 xLAM2 to 0.088 Gemini 2.5 Pro); weights are set by the authors, so the fit is partly by construction.
agent_test: Measure accuracy vs number of tools shown and parameters per call on our agent.

claim: Compressed CoT prompts cut tokens about 35% at near-equal accuracy (GSM8K 92.5 to 92.3, MATH 53.9 to 53.5, Llama-3-70B); the germane attention-weight rationale is untested. Chain of Draft (5 words per step) matches CoT on GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet at far fewer tokens, which also says length is not the active ingredient.
agent_test: Compare compressed against full CoT at matched accuracy; report token saving, not the germane story.

claim: Multi-agent division of labour (CoThinker) raised LiveBench scores in 16 of 25 Holm-corrected comparisons (GPT-5 reasoning 68.38 to 81.88) but instruction following fell (84.3 to 68.1 Flash-8B); component ablations disagree across models. Gap search found no token-matched single-agent control for CoThinker; related studies (Zhang 2025, Huang 2024) find debate-style systems lose to self-consistency at equal calls or tokens, so the CoThinker gain needs that control.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of one agent with schema vs split agents; the paper states no verified token-matched control.

claim: Unguarded LLM help can lower later unaided performance: in a preregistered RCT (nearly 1,000 students), GPT Base raised practice scores by 0.137 but cut the unaided exam by 0.054 (17%, p<.05); a guardrailed GPT Tutor (+0.361 practice) left the exam unchanged (-0.004), i.e. no harm but no gain. Students did not perceive the loss.
schema_part: G (do not offload the learning step); human-facing only
agent_test: Not agent-facing; relevant to human-in-the-loop design.

claim: Working-memory limits of LLMs resemble human limits in n-back tests (d' near 1 at n=3) and attention entropy rises with load.
agent_test: Run n-back-like tracking at several N on our agent at equal tokens.

claim: Element interactivity is a candidate handle on task difficulty beyond length; its measurement for LLMs is proposed, not validated.
agent_test: Score tasks by interacting elements and test if it predicts agent failure better than token length.

claim: Prompt-injected cognitive overload degrades safety: attack success 99.99% Claude-3-Opus, 90.95% GPT-4 on forbidden questions.
agent_test: Add an overload test to guardrail checks.

claim: Extra tokens alone are not the active ingredient in prompted CoT: same-length filler gave no gain in Lanham 2023, and 5-word drafts matched CoT at 7.6% to 8% of tokens (Chain of Draft); but length-without-content prompts did help GPT-3.5-era models (Jin 2024), and filler can help in trained small models (Pfau 2024). No study compared an explicit integration step against length-matched elaboration.
agent_test: Always run a token-matched control (same length, no integration step) before crediting an integration step.

claim: Scaffold benefit falls as base models get stronger and can reverse on some tasks: MAS gain over single agent shrank from about 10% to 3% (HumanEval +10.7 to +3.0), CoT lost up to 36.3 points for o1-preview vs GPT-4o on implicit learning, and plain models beat reasoning models at low complexity. Crossover location is task-dependent and not measured at equal tokens.
agent_test: Run each scaffold stage with an off switch and measure on easy and hard items separately for the actual model.

claim: Debate and self-revision stages lose to plain self-consistency at equal responses or tokens on the models tested (GSM8K GPT-3.5: SC 85.3 at 6 responses vs debate 83.2; GPT-3.5 changed correct answers to wrong ones more than the reverse); heterogeneity of models, not talking, is what adds (Heter-SoM +6.4%).
schema_part: revision stage needs an external verifier
agent_test: Do not add a self-review stage without a verifier; compare against SC at the same token budget.
audit_note: Huang 2024 Table (GSM8K GPT-3.5: SC 85.3 at 6 vs debate 83.2) and Zhang 2025 Heter-SoM +6.4% (over SoM-Average; only +5.8% over CoT-Average) match; 'heterogeneity not talking' is the Zhang position, mildly interpretive.

claim: A difficulty gate learned from the model's own hidden state is cheap and gives headroom (oracle on Qwen3-4B MATH 98.0 at 1279 tokens vs 96.2 at 2662), but is tested only on 1.5B-8B models and shows a large loss when the Easy strategy is applied to hard items (AIME24 16.7 vs 60.0).
agent_test: Use a check-and-escalate cascade (try cheap, escalate on failed check) rather than a pre-classified gate until a frontier-model test exists.
